data.name: Ganraj
data.gender_notes: Ganraj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ganraj is a name derived from Sanskrit, which means 'Lord of Ganas'. Ganas refer to the celestial attendants or guards of Lord Shiva. The name Ganraj signifies power, strength, and protection, as Lord Shiva is considered to be the supreme god of all these qualities. The name Ganraj carries the meaning “Lord of Ganas” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ganraj usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of ganas and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine presence and protection of Lord Shiva.
data.etymology: Ganraj belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Ganas.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ganraj total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ganraj holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism, reflecting the deep reverence for Lord Shiva and his power. The name Ganraj is often seen as a powerful and auspicious name, associated with strength, leadership, and guardianship. In Hindu mythology, the Ganas are often depicted as the fierce protectors of Lord Shiva and the universe.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Ganraj signifies a deep connection to Lord Shiva and the divine attributes of power, strength, and protection. It serves as a reminder of the inner strength and resilience that we possess, and the role we can play as protectors and leaders in our own lives and in the lives of others. The name also represents a deep faith and devotion to Lord Shiva, and the belief that he is the supreme guardian and protector of all beings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ganraj: Lord of the Ganas (celestial beings). Embodiment of joy, wisdom, and strength in collective consciousness.

vedic_reference.note: The name 'Ganraj' is a compound of two words - 'Gana' meaning 'group, assembly or community' and 'Raj' meaning 'rule' or 'reign'. This name is derived from the name of Lord Ganesha, who is often referred to as the 'Lord of the Ganas' or the 'King of the Ganas'. He is the deity of wisdom, knowledge, new beginnings, and is the remover of obstacles. He is the son of Lord Shiva and Parvati, and is also known as the elephant-headed god. The name 'Ganraj' is a beautiful and meaningful name for a baby boy, and is deeply rooted in the rich cultural heritage of India.

historical_references.reference: Ganraj Chhatrapati was the last king of the Satara Maratha Confederacy, which ruled the western part of the Indian subcontinent from 1674 to 1818.
Ganraj was also known as Mahadji Shinde, as he belonged to the Shinde dynasty, a Maratha princely house that participated in the Deccan campaigns against the Mughals in the 17th and 18th centuries.
historical_references.context: Ganraj assumed the title of Chhatrapati (Emperor) in 1787 after the death of Maratha Peshwa Madhavrao II.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Ganraj continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Krishna Ganraj in Bali, Indonesia attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Ganraj, which means "Lord of Ganas". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
